description:
Follow-up of defk-zep. After safepoints spill only live locals, the Keccak round loop (a short flat loop, no safepoint inside) still has 6-11 stack stores+loads per round in the yielding kernel and 0 under yield: false; 16 MB is ~20.7 ms vs ~18.3 ms (under load). What stays live across the hot loop only in yielding kernels: defk_ticks and defk_budget (two registers where one countdown would do: DEFK_SP as (defk_left -= W) <= 0), defk_rs (read by every loop header's resume dispatch), and the short loop's rem, live across the loop only for DEFK_TICKS(rem + 1) after it (charging on entry, as flat == :exits already does, is equivalent for a plain loop and frees it; tried in defk-zep: 9 -> 7 spills in two orderings, inside noise on time). Measure with the spill counter approach in defk-zep's comment (cc -S with build.ex's cflags, count [sp] loads/stores in the loop with the most ror).

Merged from defk-w8r.1 (2026-10-20): the same bookkeeping also shows as a safepoint per outer iteration when the body holds a short inner loop. Found in defk-l2g (2026-10-15, provisional, load 4-7). With Myers bit-parallel Levenshtein, fuzzy_search's kernel spends ~4 ms per query over 234k words, a few ns per word. The fast-path report says of the word loop: 'loop: a safepoint every iteration: the body has a nested loop'. The inner Enum.reduce_while over the word's bytes runs in strips, charged on entry. examples/fuzzy_search/bench/yield_cost.exs: yielding 4.9 ms vs yield: false 4.1-4.2 ms, +19%, at ~17 yields per query; with the DP kernel it was +3.5-4.5%. A huge slice (DEFK_SLICE_US=10000000) did not change the yields or the gap, so the cost is the per-word bookkeeping, not the yields. Under load defk serves ~21% fewer req/s than the blocking build (1790-1840 vs 2260-2370).

Scope: (a) the register experiments above (single countdown; charge a plain short loop on entry), and (b) the per-iteration safepoint of an outer loop with a short inner loop: what it costs (the check, the resume dispatch, registers kept live) and a cheaper shape, for example charging the outer loop in strips by the inner loop's trip count, or one safepoint per N outer iterations. Keep the worst-case scheduler gap within the slice; the runtime contract (tick gap, yields and resume, adaptive slices from defk-04y) stays intact. Adopt a change only if spills drop and time improves beyond noise, on Keccak 16 MB and the fuzzy_search yield cost script, interleaved repeats, quiet machine or marked provisional.

Done when both breakdowns (Keccak spills, fuzzy_search per-word cost) are recorded in docs/performance.md and either a fix lands with mix test green, forced-yield tests and the tick-gap bench unchanged, or the ticket records why no fix was worth it.

> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement
**Summary:** Experiment: cut the registers yield bookkeeping keeps live in hot short loops (one countdown instead of defk_ticks + defk_budget; charge a plain short loop on entry); adopt only if it measurably helps

**Current behavior:**
In the Keccak round loop (a short flat loop, no safepoint inside), the yielding kernel keeps 6-11 stack stores+loads per round that yield: false does not have; 16 MB takes ~20.7 ms vs ~18.3 ms (under load). Live across the loop only in yielding kernels: defk_ticks and defk_budget (two registers where one countdown would do: DEFK_SP as (defk_left -= W) <= 0), defk_rs (read by every loop header's resume dispatch), and the short loop's rem, live only for DEFK_TICKS(rem + 1) after it. defk-zep tried charging on entry: 9 -> 7 spills, time inside noise.

**Desired behavior:**
- Try the single countdown, and charging a plain short loop on entry, separately and together. Measure spills (cc -S with the build's cflags, count stack loads/stores in the hottest loop, as in defk-zep's comment) and time (Keccak 16 MB and two other short-loop examples, interleaved repeats, quiet machine or marked provisional).
- Adopt a change only if spills drop and time improves beyond noise, with the runtime contract intact (tick gap unchanged, yields and resume correct, adaptive slices from defk-04y still work). Otherwise revert and record the result.
- Either way record the numbers and conclusion in docs/performance.md.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Spill counts and timings before/after per variant, in docs/performance.md
- [ ] If adopted: full suite, forced-yield tests and the tick-gap bench pass/unchanged; `mix docs`, `mix credo --strict` clean
- [ ] If not adopted: no code change merged; the report says why

**Out of scope:**
- Changing safepoint placement or the slice length; defk_rs resume dispatch redesign (note ideas only)

Another case from defk-klw: fuzzy_search's kernel with the cut-off (Enum.reduce_while over rows, short rows) is +3.5-4.5% yielding vs yield: false, and stays +3.6-4.7% with ~0 yields (DEFK_SLICE_US=10000000), so it is per-row bookkeeping (DEFK_SP every row, resume check, strip copy of the DP loop), not yields. Before the cut-off the same kernel was -2%. Under load: 0.94-0.98x the blocking build's req/s.

title: Yield bookkeeping in hot short loops: Keccak spills 6-11 per round, and fuzzy_search Myers pays a safepoint per word (+19%)
